Appeals Court Ruling Offers Trump Path to Move Hush Money Case

A federal appeals court has provided former President Donald Trump a potential path to move his hush money conviction case to federal court. The panel ordered a lower court to promptly decide if the case belongs in federal jurisdiction. If successful, Trump could then argue for the verdict to be discarded based on presidential immunity. Separately, Trump criticized California Governor Gavin Newsom's decision to commute the death sentences of 548 prisoners, calling it a 'shocking act of injustice' and showing mercy to 'the most evil monsters.' Newsom defended his commutation plan amid the backlash.
